h1: The 5 Best Glass Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Glass Air Fryers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 5 best glass air fryers of 2026, from Ninja Crispi to Cuisinart and Kismile, compared by modes, size and price bucket.
summary: The Ninja Crispi Pro, a 6-in-1 glass air fryer, is the best here for cooks who want the widest feature set. The 4-in-1 Crispi is the balanced buy, and the Cuisinart ClearView suits one or two people with a 4 Qt basket. The Kismile is the low-cost way into glass.
intro: The appeal of a glass air fryer is simple: you can see the food browning without pulling the basket and dumping the heat you just built up. That sounds like a gimmick until you cook something thin, like bacon or breaded cutlets, where thirty seconds too long is the difference between crisp and dry. The catch is that glass models vary widely in size, modes and price, and titles rarely say which differences matter.

We ranked five glass air fryers using only what their listings give: function count, capacity, model number and price bucket. Where a listing is thin, as with the DualZone and the Kismile, we say so. Glass also changes care, since it can chip or crack if mishandled, so read the manual before treating one like a steel basket.

products.name: Ninja Crispi Pro Glass Air Fryer
products.verdict: The widest feature set among glass models here.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi Pro is a glass air fryer with six functions, model AS101LG, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Six modes mean it does more than air fry: it can take on jobs beyond crisping, which is the argument for paying more than the cheaper glass fryers. The glass cooking vessel keeps food visible throughout.

It ranks above the 4-in-1 Crispi because it adds two more functions. That is its entire edge, and it is the reason to pay the extra bucket. Listing detail beyond the function count is thin.

Buy it if you want one appliance to do the most. The caveats are the price bracket and the question of whether you will actually use six modes. If you only air fry and reheat, the 4-in-1 below does the same cooking for less.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want maximum function in glass.
products.skipIf: You only want to air fry on a budget.

products.name: Ninja Crispi Glass Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 4-in-1 glass fryer in the middle price bucket.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi, model FN101GY, is a 4-in-1 glass air fryer in the $100 to $200 bucket. Four functions cover the handful of jobs most cooks hand an air fryer, without paying for modes that rarely get used. The glass body lets you check browning without opening it.

It ranks below the Pro because it has two fewer functions, but above the other picks because Ninja's four-mode design offers a wider spread than the single-purpose models. It also costs a full bucket less than the Pro, which makes the value case clear for most households.

Buy it if you want a Crispi without the premium price. The caveat: other listings of this line come in different colors and model numbers, so check that FN101GY is what you are ordering. The listing otherwise gives little detail.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a balanced glass fryer.

products.name: Ninja Crispi DualZone Glass Countertop Air Fryer
products.verdict: The DualZone name points to two cooking zones.
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi DualZone is a glass countertop air fryer, model DD101IV2, in the $200 to $500 bucket. The DualZone name points to two cooking zones, which would let you cook two foods at once, but the listing data does not spell out capacity or function count.

It ranks third because the Pro costs the same bucket and states six functions, so the DualZone has to justify itself with unlisted detail. Dual-zone designs are attractive for cooking a main and a side at the same time without flavors crossing, though glass dual designs carry the same fragility as single ones.

Buy it if you are curious about dual cooking and will confirm the specs on the live page. Skip it if you need verified capacity numbers. Check whether both zones are glass before ordering, because the listing is not explicit.
products.idealFor: Ninja fans interested in the DualZone design.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 4 Qt glass basket with a ClearView window.
products.description:
The Cuisinart air fryer has a glass basket, a ClearView window, five functions and a stated 4 Qt capacity, in the $100 to $200 bucket. The window and glass basket together give the same watch-while-it-cooks view as the Ninja glass models, in a more familiar shape.

It ranks below the Ninja picks because 4 Qt is a smaller basket, and the Kismile beats it on capacity at a lower price. Its five functions sit between the Crispi's four and the Pro's six. The stated capacity is a plus in a field of vague listings.

Buy it for one or two people who like to watch their food. Skip it if you cook for a crowd, since a 4 Qt basket needs batches for a family. The honest caveat is size: it will not hold a whole chicken or a large tray of wings.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples who like watching food cook.

products.name: Kismile 5QT Glass Air Fryer
products.description:
The Kismile is a 5QT glass air fryer in the $50 to $100 bucket, the lowest price band in the ranking. A 5QT glass basket is larger than the Cuisinart's 4 Qt, which gives it more room per batch than its price suggests.

It ranks last because the listing gives no function count or other features. You are buying capacity and glass, and little else is documented. A lesser-known brand also means less certainty about parts and support, and glass makes replacement parts more valuable if a basket breaks.

Buy it if you want glass on a budget and will cook simple things like fries and nuggets. Skip it if you want documented presets or a brand with a dealer network. Read the product page for wattage and warranty before ordering.
products.idealFor: Budget shoppers wanting a glass fryer.

whatMatters.detail: Function count is the number of cooking modes, such as air fry, roast and reheat. A 4-in-1 or 6-in-1 label tells you how many appliances it replaces. Look for the number in the title and confirm which modes are included, since some listings count basic settings as modes. More modes only help if you will switch between them.

Capacity is measured in quarts and tells you how much food fits. A 4 Qt basket suits one or two people, while 5QT feeds a little more. Check the quart size in the title, and compare it to the batch you cook, since overcrowding a basket stops food from crisping.

A glass basket or window lets you watch browning without opening the unit and losing heat. Look for glass named in the listing, like the Cuisinart's ClearView window. Remember glass is more fragile than metal, so check the manual for handling advice and avoid thermal shocks such as washing a hot basket under cold water.

Ninja sells the Crispi under identical names with different model numbers and colors. Confirm the model, like FN101GY or AS101LG, before ordering, because specs and function counts differ between them. Check the model number in the title and in the product details, not only the photo, since colors and lookalike boxes cause most mix-ups.

Glass models span from the $50 to $100 bucket to $200 to $500, and higher tiers add modes and zones. Match the price to the features you will actually use. Check the live price before buying, since Ninja air fryers are discounted often and the gap between tiers can shift. Wait for a sale if the Pro is your target.

faq.q: Why choose glass over a regular air fryer?
faq.a: You can watch food without opening the unit. That keeps heat in and helps avoid overcooking, especially thin foods that go from golden to dry quickly. The Cuisinart's ClearView window and the Ninja glass bodies both offer this.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with the Ninja Crispi?
faq.a: They mix up model numbers. Several Crispi listings share a name but differ by model and color, so confirm FN101GY, AS101LG or DD101IV2 against the function count you want, and not just the photo.

faq.q: Is the Crispi Pro worth it over the 4-in-1?
faq.a: If you will use six functions, yes. Otherwise the 4-in-1 Crispi in the $100 to $200 bucket is the better value, and it still gives a glass body and a broad mode range, so most households lose very little.
It lists a 4 Qt capacity, which suits one or two people. The Kismile lists 5QT, so it holds more per batch, but it has less documented detail than the Cuisinart.

faq.q: How do I clean a glass air fryer?
faq.a: Check the manual for dishwasher safety and avoid abrasive pads on glass. Let the basket cool before washing, because sudden temperature changes can crack glass baskets like the Ninja's.

faq.q: Does the DualZone have two baskets?
faq.a: The name suggests two zones, but the listing does not give details, so confirm on the product page. Capacity and function count are unstated, which is why it ranks below the Pro. Ask the seller before ordering if two baskets are essential.

finalTake: Buy the Ninja Crispi Pro if you will use six modes and accept the $200 to $500 price. The 4-in-1 Crispi is the sensible default for most kitchens. The Cuisinart fits small households, and the Kismile covers a budget. Always confirm the model number, because Crispi listings repeat names with different codes.
